body: Africa World Airlines (AWA) is putting the Embraer E190 at the center of its plan to expand across underserved markets in West Africa, shifting to a hub-and-spoke model centered on Accra that prioritizes reliable regional connectivity over serving as many points as possible with a limited fleet. Chief Operating Officer Sohail Mahmood set out the strategy in an interview at the Aviation Africa Summit in Nairobi on September 9 and 10, 2026.

The fleet shift is substantial: AWA previously relied mainly on 50-seat Embraer ERJ-145s, while the new E190 seats 102 passengers, more than doubling capacity per aircraft. The first E190 arrived in Accra on September 19, 2026, a second is expected before the end of the year, and the airline reportedly aims to grow the E190 fleet to as many as 10 aircraft within 18 to 24 months. The Accra–Abidjan route resumed on August 31, 2026, restoring a link suspended during the COVID-19 pandemic, with four flights per week.

Mahmood's reasoning is that demand in West Africa is spread across many cities, and some routes cannot support the capacity of a larger narrowbody aircraft, making the E190 a fitting successor to the ERJ-145 that can open new revenue opportunities and underserved destinations without capacity that is hard to fill every day. The priority is to consolidate West Africa and connect its coastal cities first, then expand into Central and East Africa, using interline partnerships with southern African carriers to extend the network without operating every route itself, with the long-term goal of a pan-African network that also addresses the high cost of air travel in Africa.
en.summary: Africa World Airlines is building its West Africa expansion around the 102-seat Embraer E190, replacing its 50-seat ERJ-145s under an Accra-centered hub-and-spoke strategy, with the first E190 delivered in September 2026.
en.title: Africa World Airlines bets on Embraer E190s to connect West Africa

body: 非洲世界航空（Africa World Airlines，AWA）將巴西航空工業E190置於拓展西非服務不足市場計畫的核心，策略轉向以阿克拉為中心的樞紐輻射模式，著重可靠的區域連結，而非在機隊規模有限下盡可能連結更多地點。營運長Sohail Mahmood在2026年9月9日至10日於奈洛比舉行的Aviation Africa Summit受訪時說明了這項策略。
機隊轉變幅度不小：AWA過去主要使用50座的巴西航空工業ERJ-145，新引進的E190為102座，單機載客量逾一倍。首架E190於2026年9月19日抵達阿克拉，第二架預計於年底前交付，公司據報目標在未來18至24個月內將E190機隊擴充至最多10架。阿克拉—阿必尚航線已於2026年8月31日復航，恢復因COVID-19疫情而中斷的連結，每週四班。

Mahmood認為選機須符合西非市場現實：需求分散於眾多城市，部分航線難以支撐較大型窄體客機的運能，E190是ERJ-145的合理後繼機型，可在不承擔難以每日維持的運能下，開拓新收益機會與服務不足的目的地。優先順序為先鞏固西非、連結西非沿岸主要城市，再拓展至中非與東非，並透過與南部非洲業者的聯運合作延伸網絡，而無須自行營運每條航線，長期目標是建立連結全非洲的網絡，並處理非洲航空旅行成本偏高的問題。
zh.summary: 非洲世界航空以102座的巴西航空工業E190為核心推動西非擴張，取代50座的ERJ-145，採阿克拉樞紐輻射策略，首架E190已於2026年9月交付。
zh.title: 非洲世界航空押注巴西航空工業E190連結西非
